scenario: Scenario 1: Peer withdrawal inside a listing window
notes: The check is reachable on the pinned tree with no fault: LeaderElectionSupport.toLeaderOffers lists offers with getChildren, then reads each with a separate getData and does not tolerate a vanished child, so a peer's stop() delete served between those calls makes FinalRequestProcessor.java:674 throw NoNodeException on the server; the client then goes FAILED with its offer still live and the library never retries. MC-1 is the primary result because it needs only concurrency, and its frame was captured by a read-only JDI watcher in a same-module variant of the workload using the public API with no source changes (repro/MC-1-jdi.frames, also seen in the unmodified workload in repro/MC-1-workload.frames, where the tests still passed). Two further TargetSafe findings were also reproduced with the same frame and root cause: MC-2 (INTERLEAVING: a participant's own stop() racing its EventThread re-determination, repro/test_bugMC-2_selfstop.sh) and MC-3 (FAULT: another session's close() or real expiry, repro/test_bugMC-3_second_session_end.sh). Bounds: each BFS stopped at its first violation, so these are distinct-state counts up to that point and not exhaustive counts; diameter is TLC's reported search depth. MC_probe_s2_selfstop.cfg is an attribution probe with the MC_hunt_s2.cfg bounds and the restricted invariant TargetSafeSelfStop, added because the S2 hunt stopped first at a peerStop firing (realization S1-ii of MC-1). Under the workload bounds, MC.cfg exhausted 86473 distinct states at depth 48 with no violation. The three validated traces contain no firing or open race window. Reproductions ran on a standalone server, and MC-1 ran on one shared handle, so a real quorum was not tested.
